# dyf

> Index embedding spaces and see their structure. Builds a density-based LSH tree over
> your embeddings, writes it to a `.dyf` file that opens in ~5 ms without loading data,
> searches it with a Rust kernel, and exposes the topology that tree discovers along the
> way — which regions are dense, which items bridge between concepts, which are unique.

Python package, MIT, pre-v1. `pip install dyf`.

**Not** competing to be the fastest ANN retriever — mature graph libraries (HNSW,
pynndescent) win on the pure recall-vs-latency frontier. dyf's strengths are structure
discovery, hierarchy, instant-open on-disk indexes, and reaching exact recall on a single
index by raising `nprobe`.

Two things worth knowing before reading further:

- The package has over a hundred public names. Do not scan them — run `dyf api` or
  `dyf.overview()`, which groups them with an entry point per group.
- `dyf info <file.dyf>` describes an index without loading it (~0.09 s on a 479 MB,
  229k-item file), and `--json` makes it parseable. That is the cheapest way to learn what
  an artifact contains.

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://dyf.io/getting-started.html): installation, the typical
  build-index-search path, and code recipes for each major feature.
- [How it works](https://dyf.io/how-it-works.html): the two-stage PCA-based LSH algorithm,
  the metrics it produces, and what Dense / Bridge / Orphan actually mean.
- [API reference](https://dyf.io/reference/): every public class and function.
- [README](https://github.com/jdonaldson/dyf/blob/main/README.md): the fastest orientation,
  including the CLI and the measured performance table.

## Command line

Exit codes are a contract: `0` success, `1` a normal negative answer (nothing found, graph
stale), `2` a bad request, `3` a missing dependency or unreachable service. Error messages
name what to install or start.

- `dyf info f.dyf [--json]`: describe an index without loading it.
- `dyf api [group] [--json]`: grouped map of the Python API.
- `dyf index-source|index-images|index-video`: build a `.dyf` from a source tree, an image
  directory, or a video. Add `--dry-run` to see counts and cost first — it embeds nothing
  and writes nothing.
- `dyf concepts build|query|check|list`: a concept graph over your own markdown notes.

The `index-*` commands are CLI-only and deliberately absent from `__all__`; from Python,
build embeddings yourself and call `write_lazy_index`.

## Optional

- [dyfviz](https://github.com/jdonaldson/dyfviz): enrichment and the browser tour — UMAP
  projection, Louvain clustering, LLM labelling, narration, TTS. Split out of dyf in 0.13.
  It reads and rewrites `.dyf` files; nothing in dyf depends on it.
- [dyf-rs](https://pypi.org/project/dyf-rs/): the Rust kernel behind search. Results are
  bit-identical to the pure-Python reference.
- [Changelog](https://github.com/jdonaldson/dyf/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): pre-v1, so the API
  breaks freely between releases; this is where it is recorded.
- [Known issues](https://github.com/jdonaldson/dyf/blob/main/KNOWN_ISSUES.md): open defects
  in the library surface, kept honest — including features that ship but do not work.
